paper.title: GW170817: Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Neutron Star Inspiral
paper.authors: The LIGO Scientific Collaboration, The Virgo Collaboration

thesis: This unprecedented joint gravitational and electromagnetic observation provides insight into astrophysics, dense matter, gravitation and cosmology.

reconstruction.scope: abstract-level graph with retained full text

nodes.title: Research question
nodes.body: What phenomenon is supported by the reported observations?

nodes.title: Choose instrument and selection
nodes.body: On August 17, 2017 at 12:41:04 UTC the Advanced LIGO and Advanced Virgo gravitational-wave detectors made their first observation of a binary neutron star inspiral.

nodes.title: Acquire and analyze observations
nodes.body: The source was localized within a sky region of 28 deg$^2$ (90% probability) and had a luminosity distance of $40^{+8}_{-14}$ Mpc, the closest and most precisely localized gravitational-wave signal yet.

nodes.title: Primary reported result
nodes.body: The association with the gamma-ray burst GRB 170817A, detected by Fermi-GBM 1.7 s after the coalescence, corroborates the hypothesis of a neutron star merger and provides the first direct evidence of a link between these mergers and short gamma-ray bursts.

nodes.title: Published conclusion
nodes.body: This unprecedented joint gravitational and electromagnetic observation provides insight into astrophysics, dense matter, gravitation and cosmology.
